pulls.title: 8390031: vmTestbase/nsk/jdb/suspend/suspend001 hangs with virtual test threads after suspend/cont
pulls.author: shivshah-oracle
pulls.body_excerpt: Converts suspend001 to ThreadWrapper and fixes the hang. The test assumed MyThread always grabs the shared lock first once main releases it, which isn't guaranteed. With virtual threads the single wakeup goes to the first thread that blocked, that's Suspended, and a suspended virtual thread can't mount, so MyThread was never woken and the debuggee stalled. Now each thread gates on its own lock so nothing depends on who gets the wakeup. pulls.author: PeyaPeyaPeyang
pulls.body_excerpt: Enhances `FileServerHandler` in the jdk.httpserver module to support the `Range` header. This change contains: 1. A new constant `HTTP_RANGE_NOT_SATISFIABLE` to the `Code` to indicate unsatisifiable ranges. 2. `Accept-Ranges: bytes` for all file retrievals. 3. Single `bytes` ranges, returning `206 Partial Content` with `Content-Range`. 4. Multiple `bytes` ranges with `multipart/byteranges`. 5. Sorting and merging of overlapping or adjacent ranges. pulls.title: 8388417: Support VerifyOops for AOT caching stub and code
pulls.author: vnkozlov
pulls.body_excerpt: Main reason VerifyOops was not supported with AOT code is that we used fixed size table for C strings referenced from code to cache them. Verify oops code generated a lot of C strings which overflow that table. The fix is to use growableArray during AOT assembly phase to collect C strings referenced from AOT code (stubs, adapters). During production run C heap array will be used to reference C strings in AOT cache because we know number of C strings. pulls.title: 8389677: RISC-V: Prefer vmv.v.i to zero vector registers
pulls.author: zangcq
pulls.body_excerpt: The RISC-V Optimization Guide recommends using `vmv.v.i vd, 0` to zero a vector register instead of other idioms such as `vxor.vv vd, vd, vd` or `vmv.v.x vd, x0`. Compared with these alternatives, `vmv.v.i` is a pure immediate splat. It does not read a source vector register and does not consume a scalar register read port. As a result, it avoids the false self-dependency introduced by `vxor.vv vd, vd, vd` and the scalar register dependency of `vmv.v.x vd, x0`. pulls.author: PeyaPeyaPeyang
pulls.body_excerpt: When `left == right` is known at code generation time, the operands are necessarily the same oop, so we can jump directly to `L_oops_equal`. This patch changes both x86 and aarch65 to do that. I also considered emitting `equal_result` and returning early in that case. I decided not to do that because `LIR_OpSubstitutabilityCheck::emit_code()` still appends the slow-path stub after `emit_opSubstitutabilityCheck()` returns.
